newsitem.title: USA: Kato Kaelin offers new evidence in Simpson case.
newsitem.headline: Kato Kaelin offers new evidence in Simpson case.

text.p: Brian "Kato" Kaelin, O.J. Simpson's one-time house guest, offered new evidence in the former football star's civil trial on Tuesday, telling the jury about a movie sex scene and thumps he heard in the night.

Kaelin described the thumps he heard on the night of June 12, 1994, when Simpson's ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend Ronald Goldman, were murdered, as being "like someone falling back behind my bedroom wall."
Kaelin also testified he and Simpson watched a video that afternoon that contained a scene involving oral sex and which Simpson compared to an act he had witnessed his wife performing on another man.

Kaelin became a minor celebrity when he testified at Simpson's criminal trial, but at that time did not describe the now-famous thumps as being made by a person. Instead he said he thought they might have been made by an earthquake as they caused a picture on his wall to move.
A bloody glove matching one found at the murder scene was discovered in an alley behind Simpson's mansion where Kaelin said he had heard three loud thumps.

Police claimed the thumps were made by Simpson as he jumped over a fence onto his property after committing the murders outside Nicole Brown Simpson's home two miles (three km) away. But his criminal defence team contended the glove was planted by Detective Mark Fuhrman, who they painted as a racist, rogue cop out to frame Simpson.
Simpson was found not guilty of the murders in October 1995 and is now fighting the wrongful death lawsuit brought by the victims' families, who are seeking financial damages.
Kaelin's testimony about watching a sex scene in the movie, "The World According to Garp," was also the first mention made of the incident.

He said Simpson invited him into the mansion to watch the scene. "The wife was going to give oral sex in the car and he (Simpson) compared that to seeing Nicole give oral sex at (her) house; that he was outside (the house) and he saw Nicole doing it to a gentleman named Keith."

The jury in the wrongful death civil case also heard a secretly taped conversation in which Nicole Brown Simpson told police she feared Simpson might kill her when he burst into her home on Oct. 25, 1993.
"I always felt if it happened one more time it would be the last time," she told officers, explaining why she had called the police emergency number.

On the audiotape made while Simpson was still in Nicole Brown Simpson's home that night, with a tape recorder hidden in the pocket of Sgt. Craig Lally, Nicole Brown Simpson said Simpson "gets this animalistic look to him and I get scared when he looks like that."
The tape was not played to the jury in his criminal trial.
Simpson is heard on the tape expressing surprise that his then-estranged wife had called the police. "We were yelling at each other but I'm surprised she called the cops."
Asked what started the fight, he said "An ex-boyfriend." Later Simpson said, "I didn't want this guy in her life."
